NASB.1: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took the ark of the LORD and brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.
NASB.2: From the day that the ark remained at Kiriath-jearim, the time was long, for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
NASB.3: Then Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, 'If you return to the LORD with all your heart, remove the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you and direct your hearts to the LORD and serve Him alone; and He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.'
NASB.4: So the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth and served the LORD alone.
NASB.5: Then Samuel said, 'Gather all Israel to Mizpah and I will pray to the LORD for you.'
NASB.6: They gathered to Mizpah, and drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day and said there, 'We have sinned against the LORD.' And Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.
NASB.7: Now when the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered to Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the sons of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
NASB.8: Then the sons of Israel said to Samuel, 'Do not cease to cry to the LORD our God for us, that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines.'
NASB.9: Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it for a whole burnt offering to the LORD; and Samuel cried to the LORD for Israel and the LORD answered him.
NASB.10: Now Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, and the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day against the Philistines and confused them, so that they were routed before Israel.
NASB.11: The men of Israel went out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.
NASB.12: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and named it Ebenezer, saying, 'Thus far the LORD has helped us.'
NASB.13: So the Philistines were subdued and they did not come anymore within the border of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
NASB.14: The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even to Gath; and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. So there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
NASB.15: Now Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
NASB.16: He used to go annually on circuit to Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these places.
NASB.17: Then his return [was] to Ramah, for his house [was] there, and there he judged Israel; and he built there an altar to the LORD.

NKJV.1: Then the men of Kirjath Jearim came and took the ark of the LORD, and brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.
NKJV.2: So it was that the ark remained in Kirjath Jearim a long time; it was there twenty years. And all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
NKJV.3: Then Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you return to the LORD with all your hearts, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtoreths from among you, and prepare your hearts for the LORD, and serve Him only; and He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.”
NKJV.4: So the children of Israel put away the Baals and the Ashtoreths, and served the LORD only.
NKJV.5: And Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”
NKJV.6: So they gathered together at Mizpah, drew water, and poured it out before the LORD. And they fasted that day, and said there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the children of Israel at Mizpah.
NKJV.7: Now when the Philistines heard that the children of Israel had gathered together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the children of Israel heard of it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
NKJV.8: So the children of Israel said to Samuel, “Do not cease to cry out to the LORD our God for us, that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”
NKJV.9: And Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. Then Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.
NKJV.10: Now as Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a loud thunder upon the Philistines that day, and so confused them that they were overcome before Israel.
NKJV.11: And the men of Israel went out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and drove them back as far as below Beth Car.
NKJV.12: Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”
NKJV.13: So the Philistines were subdued, and they did not come anymore into the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
NKJV.14: Then the cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath; and Israel recovered its territory from the hands of the Philistines. Also there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
NKJV.15: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
NKJV.16: He went from year to year on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and judged Israel in all those places.
NKJV.17: But he always returned to Ramah, for his home was there. There he judged Israel, and there he built an altar to the LORD.

ESV.1: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of the LORD and brought it to the house of Abinadab on the hill. And they consecrated his son Eleazar to have charge of the ark of the LORD.
ESV.2: From the day that the ark was lodged at Kiriath-jearim, a long time passed, some twenty years, and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
ESV.3: And Samuel said to all the house of Israel, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you and direct your heart to the LORD and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”
ESV.4: So the people of Israel put away the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and they served the LORD only.
ESV.5: Then Samuel said, “Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”
ESV.6: So they gathered at Mizpah and drew water and poured it out before the LORD and fasted on that day and said there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the people of Israel at Mizpah.
ESV.7: Now when the Philistines heard that the people of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the people of Israel heard of it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
ESV.8: And the people of Israel said to Samuel, “Do not cease to cry out to the LORD our God for us, that he may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”
ESV.9: So Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. And Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.
ESV.10: As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to attack Israel. But the LORD thundered with a mighty sound that day against the Philistines and threw them into confusion, and they were defeated before Israel.
ESV.11: And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines and struck them, as far as below Beth-car.
ESV.12: Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen  and called its name Ebenezer;  for he said, “Till now the LORD has helped us.”
ESV.13: So the Philistines were subdued and did not again enter the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
ESV.14: The cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. There was peace also between Israel and the Amorites.
ESV.15: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
ESV.16: And he went on a circuit year by year to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah. And he judged Israel in all these places.
ESV.17: Then he would return to Ramah, for his home was there, and there also he judged Israel. And he built there an altar to the LORD.

WEB.1: The men of Kiriath Jearim came, and took Yahweh’s ark, and brought it into Abinadab’s house on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep Yahweh’s ark.
WEB.2: From the day that the ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim, the time was long; for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after Yahweh.
WEB.3: Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to Yahweh with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts to Yahweh, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”
WEB.4: Then the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served Yahweh only.
WEB.5: Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to Yahweh for you.”
WEB.6: They gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water, and poured it out before Yahweh, and fasted on that day, and said there, “We have sinned against Yahweh.” Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
WEB.7: When the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the children of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
WEB.8: The children of Israel said to Samuel, “Don’t stop crying to Yahweh our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.”
WEB.9: Samuel took a suckling lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt offering to Yahweh. Samuel cried to Yahweh for Israel; and Yahweh answered him.
WEB.10: As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines came near to battle against Israel; but Yahweh thundered with a great thunder on that day on the Philistines, and confused them; and they were struck down before Israel.
WEB.11: The men of Israel went out of Mizpah, and pursued the Philistines, and struck them, until they came under Beth Kar.
WEB.12: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer,  saying, “Yahweh helped us until now.”
WEB.13: So the Philistines were subdued, and they stopped coming within the border of Israel. Yahweh’s hand was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
WEB.14: The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even to Gath; and Israel recovered its border out of the hand of the Philistines. There was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
WEB.15: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
WEB.16: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.
WEB.17: His return was to Ramah, for his house was there; and he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to Yahweh there.

NLT.1: So the men of Kiriath-jearim came to get the Ark of the LORD. They took it to the hillside home of Abinadab and ordained Eleazar, his son, to be in charge of it.
NLT.2: The Ark remained in Kiriath-jearim for a long time — twenty years in all. During that time all Israel mourned because it seemed the LORD had abandoned them.
NLT.3: Then Samuel said to all the people of Israel, “If you want to return to the LORD with all your hearts, get rid of your foreign gods and your images of Ashtoreth. Turn your hearts to the LORD and obey him alone; then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
NLT.4: So the Israelites got rid of their images of Baal and Ashtoreth and worshiped only the LORD.
NLT.5: Then Samuel told them, “Gather all of Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”
NLT.6: So they gathered at Mizpah and, in a great ceremony, drew water from a well and poured it out before the LORD. They also went without food all day and confessed that they had sinned against the LORD. (It was at Mizpah that Samuel became Israel’s judge.)
NLT.7: When the Philistine rulers heard that Israel had gathered at Mizpah, they mobilized their army and advanced. The Israelites were badly frightened when they learned that the Philistines were approaching.
NLT.8: “Don’t stop pleading with the LORD our God to save us from the Philistines!” they begged Samuel.
NLT.9: So Samuel took a young lamb and offered it to the LORD as a whole burnt offering. He pleaded with the LORD to help Israel, and the LORD answered him.
NLT.10: Just as Samuel was sacrificing the burnt offering, the Philistines arrived to attack Israel. But the LORD spoke with a mighty voice of thunder from heaven that day, and the Philistines were thrown into such confusion that the Israelites defeated them.
NLT.11: The men of Israel chased them from Mizpah to a place below Beth-car, slaughtering them all along the way.
NLT.12: Samuel then took a large stone and placed it between the towns of Mizpah and Jeshanah. He named it Ebenezer (which means “the stone of help”), for he said, “Up to this point the LORD has helped us!”
NLT.13: So the Philistines were subdued and didn’t invade Israel again for some time. And throughout Samuel’s lifetime, the LORD’s powerful hand was raised against the Philistines.
NLT.14: The Israelite villages near Ekron and Gath that the Philistines had captured were restored to Israel, along with the rest of the territory that the Philistines had taken. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites in those days.
NLT.15: Samuel continued as Israel’s judge for the rest of his life.
NLT.16: Each year he traveled around, setting up his court first at Bethel, then at Gilgal, and then at Mizpah. He judged the people of Israel at each of these places.
NLT.17: Then he would return to his home at Ramah, and he would hear cases there, too. And Samuel built an altar to the LORD at Ramah.

CSB17.1: So the people of Kiriath-jearim came for the ark of the LORD and took it to Abinadab’s house on the hill. <sup>ⓔ</sup> They consecrated his son Eleazar to take care of it.
CSB17.2: Time went by until twenty years had passed since the ark had been taken to Kiriath-jearim. Then the whole house of Israel longed for the LORD.
CSB17.3: Samuel told them, “If you <sup>ⓕ</sup> are returning to the LORD <sup>ⓖ</sup> with all your heart, <sup>ⓗ</sup> get rid of the foreign gods <sup>ⓘ</sup> and the Ashtoreths that are among you, dedicate yourselves to <sup>[1]</sup> the LORD, and worship only him. <sup>ⓙ</sup> Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
CSB17.4: So the Israelites removed the Baals and the Ashtoreths <sup>ⓚ</sup> and only worshiped the LORD.
CSB17.5: Samuel said, “Gather all Israel at Mizpah, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf.” <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.6: When they gathered at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out in the LORD’s presence. <sup>ⓝ</sup> They fasted that day, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and there they confessed, “We have sinned against the LORD.” <sup>ⓑ</sup> And Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
CSB17.7: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, their rulers marched up toward Israel. When the Israelites heard about it, they were afraid because of the Philistines.
CSB17.8: The Israelites said to Samuel, “Don’t stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, so that he will save us from the Philistines.”
CSB17.9: Then Samuel took a young lamb <sup>ⓒ</sup> and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD on behalf of Israel, and the LORD answered him. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.10: Samuel was offering the burnt offering as the Philistines approached to fight against Israel. The LORD thundered loudly <sup>ⓔ</sup> against the Philistines that day and threw them into such confusion that they were defeated by Israel. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.11: Then the men of Israel charged out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines striking them down all the way to a place below Beth-car.
CSB17.12: Afterward, Samuel took a stone and set it upright <sup>ⓖ</sup> between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, <sup>[2]</sup> explaining, “The LORD has helped us to this point.”
CSB17.13: So the Philistines were subdued <sup>ⓗ</sup> and <sup>[3]</sup> did not invade Israel’s territory again. <sup>ⓘ</sup> The LORD’s hand was against the Philistines all of Samuel’s life.
CSB17.14: The cities from Ekron to Gath, which they had taken from Israel, were restored; Israel even rescued their surrounding territories from Philistine control. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.
CSB17.15: Samuel judged Israel throughout his life. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.16: Every year he would go on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah and would judge Israel at all these locations.
CSB17.17: Then he would return to Ramah <sup>ⓚ</sup> because his home was there, he judged Israel there, and he built an altar to the LORD there.

AMP.1: So the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of the Lord and brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill, and they consecrated Eleazar his son to care for the ark of the Lord.
AMP.2: And from that day the ark remained in Kiriath-jearim for a very long time, for it was twenty years [until the reign of King David]; and all the house of Israel lamented (wailed) and grieved after the LORD.
AMP.3: Then Samuel said to all the house of Israel, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, remove the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth (pagan goddesses) from among you and direct your hearts to the LORD and serve Him only; and He will rescue you from the hand of the Philistines."
AMP.4: So the Israelites removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth and served the LORD alone.
AMP.5: Samuel said, "Gather all Israel together at Mizpah and I will pray to the LORD for you."
AMP.6: So they gathered at Mizpah, and drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day and said there, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
AMP.7: Now when the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, the lords (governors) of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the Israelites heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
AMP.8: And the sons of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not cease to cry out to the LORD our God for us, so that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines."
AMP.9: So Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD; and Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel and the LORD answered him.
AMP.10: As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines approached for the battle against Israel. Then the LORD thundered with a great voice that day against the Philistines and threw them into confusion, and they were defeated and fled before Israel.
AMP.11: And the men of Israel came out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them down as far as [the territory] below Beth-car.
AMP.12: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and he named it Ebenezer (stone of help), saying, "Thus far the LORD has helped us."
AMP.13: So the Philistines were subdued and they did not come anymore into Israelite territory. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
AMP.14: The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath; and Israel recovered the cities' territory from the Philistines. Also there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
AMP.15: Now Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
AMP.16: He used to go annually on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these places.
AMP.17: Then he would return to Ramah, because his home was there; and there he judged Israel, and there he built an altar to the LORD.

NIV.2:
Samuel Subdues the Philistines at Mizpah
It was a long time, twenty years in all, that the ark remained at Kiriath Jearim, and all the people of Israel mourned and sought after the Lord.
NIV.3: And Samuel said to the whole house of Israel, “If you are returning to the Lord with all your hearts, then rid yourselves of the foreign gods and the Ashtoreths and commit yourselves to the Lord and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”
NIV.4: So the Israelites put away their Baals and Ashtoreths, and served the Lord only.
NIV.5: Then Samuel said, “Assemble all Israel at Mizpah and I will intercede with the Lord for you.”
NIV.6: When they had assembled at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the Lord. On that day they fasted and there they confessed, “We have sinned against the Lord.” And Samuel was leader of Israel at Mizpah.
NIV.7: When the Philistines heard that Israel had assembled at Mizpah, the rulers of the Philistines came up to attack them. And when the Israelites heard of it, they were afraid because of the Philistines.
NIV.8: They said to Samuel, “Do not stop crying out to the Lord our God for us, that he may rescue us from the hand of the Philistines.”
NIV.9: Then Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it up as a whole burnt offering to the Lord. He cried out to the Lord on Israel’s behalf, and the Lord answered him.
NIV.10: While Samuel was sacrificing the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to engage Israel in battle. But that day the Lord thundered with loud thunder against the Philistines and threw them into such a panic that they were routed before the Israelites.
NIV.11: The men of Israel rushed out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, slaughtering them along the way to a point below Beth Car.
NIV.12: Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far has the Lord helped us.”
NIV.13:
So the Philistines were subdued and did not invade Israelite territory again.
Throughout Samuel’s lifetime, the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines.
NIV.14: The towns from Ekron to Gath that the Philistines had captured from Israel were restored to her, and Israel delivered the neighboring territory from the power of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
NIV.15: Samuel continued as judge over Israel all the days of his life.
NIV.16: From year to year he went on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging Israel in all those places.
NIV.17: But he always went back to Ramah, where his home was, and there he also judged Israel. And he built an altar there to the Lord.

MSG.1: And they did. The men of Kiriath Jearim came and got the Chest of God and delivered it to the house of Abinadab on the hill. They ordained his son, Eleazar, to take responsibility for the Chest of God.
MSG.2: From the time that the Chest came to rest in Kiriath Jearim, a long time passed—twenty years it was—and throughout Israel there was a widespread, fearful movement toward God.
MSG.3: Then Samuel addressed the house of Israel: "If you are truly serious about coming back to God, clean house. Get rid of the foreign gods and fertility goddesses, ground yourselves firmly in God, worship him and him alone, and he'll save you from Philistine oppression."
MSG.4: They did it. They got rid of the gods and goddesses, the images of Baal and Ashtoreth, and gave their exclusive attention and service to God.
MSG.5: Next Samuel said, "Get everybody together at Mizpah and I'll pray for you."
MSG.6:
So everyone assembled at Mizpah. They drew water from the wells and poured it out before God in a ritual of cleansing. They fasted all day and prayed, "We have sinned against God."
So Samuel prepared the Israelites for holy war there at Mizpah.
MSG.7: When the Philistines heard that Israel was meeting at Mizpah, the Philistine leaders went on the offensive. Israel got the report and became frightened—Philistines on the move again!
MSG.8: They pleaded with Samuel, "Pray with all your might! And don't let up! Pray to God, our God, that he'll save us from the boot of the Philistines."
MSG.9: Samuel took a young lamb not yet weaned and offered it whole as a Whole-Burnt-Offering to God. He prayed fervently to God, interceding for Israel. And God answered.
MSG.10: While Samuel was offering the sacrifice, the Philistines came within range to fight Israel. Just then God thundered, a huge thunderclap exploding among the Philistines. They panicked—mass confusion!—and ran helter-skelter from Israel.
MSG.11: Israel poured out of Mizpah and gave chase, killing Philistines right and left, to a point just beyond Beth Car.
MSG.12: Samuel took a single rock and set it upright between Mizpah and Shen. He named it "Ebenezer" (Rock of Help), saying, "This marks the place where God helped us."
MSG.13: The Philistines learned their lesson and stayed home—no more border crossings. God was hard on the Philistines all through Samuel's lifetime.
MSG.14: All the cities from Ekron to Gath that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored. Israel also freed the surrounding countryside from Philistine control. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
MSG.15: Samuel gave solid leadership to Israel his entire life.
MSG.16: Every year he went on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah. He gave leadership to Israel in each of these places.
MSG.17: But always he would return to Ramah, where he lived, and preside from there. That is where he built an altar to God.

NET.1: Then the people of Kiriath Jearim came and took the ark of the LORD; they brought it to the house of Abinadab located on the hill. They consecrated Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the LORD.
NET.2: It was quite a long time — some twenty years in all — that the ark stayed at Kiriath Jearim. All the people of Israel longed for the LORD.
NET.3: Samuel said to all the people of Israel, “If you are really turning to the LORD with all your hearts, remove from among you the foreign gods and the images of Ashtoreth. Give your hearts to the LORD and serve only him. Then he will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.”
NET.4: So the Israelites removed the Baals and images of Ashtoreth. They served only the LORD.
NET.5: Then Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf.”
NET.6: After they had assembled at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the LORD. They fasted on that day, and they confessed there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” So Samuel led the people of Israel at Mizpah.
NET.7: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, the leaders of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the Israelites heard about this, they were afraid of the Philistines.
NET.8: The Israelites said to Samuel, “Keep crying out to the LORD our God so that he may save us from the hand of the Philistines!”
NET.9: So Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. Samuel cried out to the LORD on Israel’s behalf, and the LORD answered him.
NET.10: As Samuel was offering burnt offerings, the Philistines approached to do battle with Israel. But on that day the LORD thundered loudly against the Philistines. He caused them to panic, and they were defeated by Israel.
NET.11: Then the men of Israel left Mizpah and chased the Philistines, striking them down all the way to an area below Beth Car.
NET.12: Samuel took a stone and placed it between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, saying, “Up to here the LORD has helped us.”
NET.13: So the Philistines were defeated; they did not invade Israel again. The hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
NET.14: The cities that the Philistines had captured from Israel were returned to Israel, from Ekron to Gath. Israel also delivered their territory from the control of the Philistines. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.
NET.15: So Samuel led Israel all the days of his life.
NET.16: Year after year he used to travel the circuit of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; he used to judge Israel in all of these places.
NET.17: Then he would return to Ramah, because his home was there. He also judged Israel there and built an altar to the LORD there.
